title: Clive Burr - Wikipedia
notes: Clive Ronald Burr, 8 March 1956 to 12 March 2013, English. Iron Maiden's drummer 1979 to 1982, before that a member of Samson; auditioned and joined on Dennis Stratton's recommendation; on Iron Maiden, Killers and The Number of the Beast; fired in 1982 during The Beast on the Road tour, replaced by Nicko McBrain. Co-wrote Gangland and Total Eclipse. Classic Rock, February 2011: ousted after taking a break to mourn his father's death; Dickinson's 2017 autobiography suggests conflict with Steve Harris. Then Trust (swapping places with McBrain), briefly Alcatrazz, Gogmagog (with Paul Di'Anno, Janick Gers, Neil Murray and Pete Willis), Clive Burr's Escape (later Stratus), Dee Snider's Desperado, Elixir and Praying Mantis (Captured Alive in Tokyo City, 1996). 'Burr's signature white drum kit was donated to the Hard Rock Cafe in London in 2005.' Multiple sclerosis from the late 1990s; the Clive Burr MS Trust Fund; Clive Aid (2004); died in his sleep in London of its complications. Dave Lombardo: 'his style was inspiring and the albums he recorded with Iron Maiden are touchstones of my music education'; Charlie Benante: 'the drumming on Killers inspired me to kick it up a notch'; Dave McClain: he 'brought punk rock drumming into heavy metal'; Lars Ulrich, Paul Bostaph and others cite him. Dickinson: 'the best drummer the band ever had ... Clive had this incredible feel'; Adrian Smith: 'an Ian Paice-type drummer, steady and solid with a nice feel to everything.'

title: Samson (band) - Wikipedia
notes: Formed in 1977 by Paul Samson. Chris Aylmer suggested the name and recommended 'a young drummer, Clive Burr, whom he had previously played with in the band Maya'; the first singles, Telephone and Mr Rock & Roll, in 1978; 'At the end of 1978, Burr left'. He was a member 'both before and after his tenure with Iron Maiden'.

title: Praying Mantis (band) - Wikipedia
notes: Stratus, originally 'Clive Burr's Escape': formed by Burr with the Troy brothers, Bernie Shaw and Alan Nelson; one album, Throwing Shapes.

title: Killers (Iron Maiden album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 16 February 1981 in the UK. The first with Adrian Smith and with Martin Birch producing, the last with Paul Di'Anno. Wrathchild among the first songs Steve Harris wrote; Harris: 'Production-wise, Killers was like chalk and cheese compared to the first album.' Clive Burr, drums.

title: The Number of the Beast (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 22 March 1982 (US), 29 March (UK). The first with Bruce Dickinson and the last with Clive Burr; the only Iron Maiden album with songwriting credits for Burr. Recorded at Battery Studios with Martin Birch. Total Eclipse, by Harris, Murray and Burr, a B-side.

title: Run to the Hills - Wikipedia
notes: The first single from The Number of the Beast, the first with Dickinson, credited to Steve Harris; Clive Burr on drums. Reissued in 2002 for the Clive Burr MS Trust Fund.
